questions.question: You have a tokenizer that turns text into numbers, and a text collection far larger than your machine's memory. What is the most sensible way to prepare training examples from it?
options: Read and process the files as a stream, converting a small portion at a time and discarding what you already processed.
Load every file into memory at once before doing anything else.
Delete most of the files so that whatever remains fits in memory.
Convert the text by hand one sentence at a time without writing any program.
questions.explanation: Processing a stream in small portions keeps memory use flat no matter how large the collection grows. This lesson builds a full training data pipeline on top of that idea, starting from your tokenizer output.

questions.question: Why does `tokenize_corpus` append `eos_id` to each encoded document?
options: To make every document exactly the same length.
To mark where one document ends.
To replace all padding with a trainable word.
To increase the number of ordinary BPE merges.
questions.explanation: The EOS token gives the model an explicit boundary between documents before their token IDs are packed into fixed-length sequences.

questions.question: What does `quality_filter(text, min_words=50)` return for a 12-word document, assuming no other checks matter?
options: True, because word count is only advisory.
True, after adding 38 padding words.
False: 12 words is below 50.
A MinHash signature instead of a Boolean.
questions.explanation: The first filter condition rejects documents whose `split()` word count is less than `min_words`, so 12 words fails the default threshold.

questions.question: When `deduplicate` compares two candidate documents, which result causes the later document to be removed?
options: Any shared word, regardless of frequency.
A matching MinHash signature at one band.
A larger character count in the later document.
Jaccard similarity reaches 0.8.
questions.explanation: LSH only proposes candidates; the function then computes exact shingle Jaccard similarity and removes the later item when it is at least 0.8.

questions.question: For a MinHash signature of length 128 and `bands=16`, how many signature values go into each LSH band?
questions.explanation: `lsh_buckets` uses `len(signature) // bands`, so 128 // 16 gives 8 rows per band.

questions.question: How does `minhash_signature` create the candidate values for a shingle at hash round `i`?
options: It counts the shingle's words and takes their mean.
The minimum SHA-256 value for `i:shingle`.
It assigns the shingle the document's token length.
It selects the LSH band with the most documents.
questions.explanation: Each round hashes the round index and shingle together, converts the digest to an integer, and records the minimum over the shingle set.
